text:
incident-bot: [P0] spike detected: 7x normal request rate to public generation endpoints from a small set of IPs. 5xxs increasing, error budget at 65% :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): paging. i'm on it. starting triage.

sam (sre): seeing very high QPS to /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings/batch from same ASNs. lots of identical user-agents. likely scraper farm.

maria (oncall): impact: higher latencies for some customers, a few 503s. customer-facing metrics show 2% request failures for paid routes.

kevin (prod-eng): can we do a live throttle on anonymous traffic and up quota enforcement?

ella (security): recommend immediate WAF quick-rule: block behavioural pattern + short term geo throttle for the worst ASNs. will prepare rule.

maria (oncall): assign runbook: 1) add rate-limit at edge 2) ban repeated identical UA requests for 10m 3) cap batch embeddings per IP 4) communicate to support/CS

nidhi (support): i'll draft a short status for customers and flag top 5 affected accounts.

sam (sre): applying edge rate-limit now (scaled for bursts). pushing config: `edgectl rate add --scope public --limit 30rps --burst 60 --duration 15m --tag incident-1891234567`

ops-bot: edgectl acknowledged, rule id `edge-rl-1891` created and pushed to 3 regions.

maria (oncall): good. next, temporary quota cap for token generation to reduce cost spike. can someone patch quota-service?

kevin (prod-eng): doing a soft cap on unauthenticated clients: `quotactl set --client-type unauthenticated --max-tokens 200000 --window 3600 --reason incident-1891`

ops-bot: quota updated successfully.

ella (security): WAF quick rule prepared. it's a pattern-based block for repetitive POST patterns and high token churn. deploying as "canary-block" to avoid collateral.

ella (security): rule payload:
```json
{
  "name": "canary-cred-spray-1891",
  "match": {
    "user_agent_pattern": "^(curl|python-requests|node-fetch)",
    "path_prefix": "/v1/generate",
    "repeat_count": 50,
    "time_window_sec": 60
  },
  "action": "block",
  "scope": "egress-public",
  "mode": "canary",
  "duration": 900
}
```

sam (sre): deployed canary -> logged ~600 hits in 2m, blocked ~540. latency improved by 18% in affected regions.

maria (oncall): nice. are we seeing any false positives?

ella (security): so far none in canary. expanding to full-block on that rule for the two worst ASNs. adding exception for our verified customers and service accounts.

ops-bot: waf rule `canary-cred-spray-1891` -> `blocked-1891` expanded to regions: us-east1, eu-west1.

kevin (prod-eng): disabling the public batch embeddings endpoint temporarily. command: `adminctl route disable /v1/embeddings/batch --reason "mitigation-1891"`

ops-bot: route disabled. healthchecks updated.

nidhi (support): sent proactive note to top 5 affected customers: flagged potential delay in embeddings and generation. keeping them updated.

maria (oncall): logging mitigation timeline for postmortem. current actions: edge rate-limit, quota cap, waf block expanded, batch endpoint disabled.

sam (sre): metrics: 70% drop in malicious QPS, 12% tail latency improvement, error rate back down to baseline for premium routes.

kevin (prod-eng): run a short-lived traffic-shaping policy to prioritize authenticated requests: `trafficctl shape --priority authenticated:1,unauthenticated:0.7 --duration 20m`

ops-bot: traffic shaping applied.

ella (security): recommending follow-up: 1) add IP/ASN long-term blocks 2) integrate UA fingerprinting rule into WAF 3) consider challenge (captcha) for suspicious sessions

maria (oncall): agree. for now, keep the temporary rules for 1 hour then reassess. I'll hand off to morning oncall in 40m.

nidhi (support): collecting customer logs and sharing with security for false-positive checks.

sam (sre): saving snapshots and config diffs: `git diff --staged` & `deployctl snapshot --tag incident-1891`.

maria (oncall): handoff to @kevin in 40. current status: mitigations active, customer impact limited to some embedding delays, monitoring for rinse/repeat.

kevin (prod-eng): ack — i'll watch the metrics and coordinate long-term mitigations.

ops-bot: incident-bot autopage will silence for 30m for this thread per oncall update.

maria (oncall): thanks team. will write a short incident summary and action items after shift. :thumbsup:

nidhi (support): noted, will update status page if anything changes.

ella (security): collecting WAF logs to submit to intel for blocking list updates.

sam (sre): follow-up tickets created: PROJ-1152 (permanent WAF rules), PROJ-1153 (embeddings auth enforcement), PROJ-1154 (UA fingerprinting).

kevin (prod-eng): good. ending handoff.

incident-bot: incident 1891234567 status -> mitigated (monitoring).
